sources.title: Comparison of Cumulative Live Birth Rates Between Fresh and Vitrified Donor Oocytes
sources.claim: Cumulative live birth rates were 69.6% with fresh and 66.7% with vitrified donor eggs (214 recipient cycles), no significant difference.
sources.quote: Cumulative live birth rates, including pregnancies from second and third embryo transfers, were 69.6% in Group A and 66.7% in Group B, with no statistically significant difference (p>0.05).

sources.title: Frozen autologous and donor oocytes are associated with differences in clinical and neonatal outcomes compared with fresh oocytes: a SART CORS analysis
sources.claim: Across 14,972 US donor egg cycles with fresh transfer, frozen donor eggs had a lower likelihood of live birth than fresh donor eggs (aRR 0.81).
sources.quote: we observed a decrease in LB (aRR 0.81, 95% CI 0.77-0.85)

sources.title: Is the risk of preeclampsia higher in donor oocyte pregnancies? A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.claim: Six cohort studies (37,994 pregnancies): egg donation associated with higher preeclampsia risk than IVF with own eggs (OR 4.50) in singleton pregnancies.
sources.quote: OR 4.50; 95% CI: 3.28-6.19; p<0.0001 ... Oocyte donation is associated with increased risk of preeclampsia in singleton pregnancies.

sources.title: MicroRNAs, small regulatory elements with significant effects on human implantation: a review
sources.journal: Journal of Assisted Reproduction and Genetics
sources.claim: Endometrial glands secrete hsa-miR-30d during the implantation window; the embryo's trophoblast takes it up and it may modify the embryo's gene expression (based on Vilella et al. 2015). Preliminary.
sources.quote: the human endometrial glands secrete hsa-miR-30d ... the embryo trophoblast took up both forms of hsa-miR-30d from the endometrial fluid ... may modify the embryo transcriptome

sources.title: Egg Donation patient fact sheet (ASRM, revised 2023)
sources.claim: Donors usually 21-34 with infectious, genetic and psychological screening; recipient takes estrogen then progesterone; transfer 3-5 days after fertilization; success not considered related to recipient age; SART/CDC 2020 average birth rate 53.5% per transfer with fresh donor eggs; counseling recommended.
sources.quote: usually between the ages of 21 and 34 ... is not considered to be related to the recipient's age ... 53.5% per embryo transfer
